bank.probe: Is there a painless black scab or crusted ulcer anywhere on the body, including the groin, armpit or waistline?
Does the fever come with violent shaking chills followed by drenching sweats, returning at roughly the same time every second day?
Did you wade through flood water, mud or a pond, or handle animals, during or after the trip?
Does the headache sit behind the eyes and get worse when you move your eyes?
Has any rash, flushing or red blotching appeared on the skin, even briefly?
Are the whites of the eyes red or bloodshot without any discharge or itching?
Are the calf muscles unusually painful or tender to press?
Did the fever climb a little higher each day over the first week rather than spiking and falling?
Have the bowels been unusually constipated, with the abdomen feeling bloated or distended?
Are there tender swollen glands in the neck, armpits or groin?
Were you bitten by mosquitoes mainly during the daytime, indoors or around the house?
Did you sit, walk or lie in tall grass, scrub or bushes, or work in fields during the trip?
Is there a cough, or any breathlessness when walking or climbing stairs?
Is there a sore throat, a blocked or runny nose?
Is anyone at home, at work or among your travel companions ill with a similar fever?
Has there been any bleeding from the gums or nose, or unusual bruising?
Has the urine turned dark, like tea or cola?
Have the eyes or skin turned yellow?
Has the amount of urine dropped noticeably in the last day?
Is there severe or worsening pain in the abdomen, especially on the right side under the ribs?
Is the vomiting persistent, three or more times in a day, or is it impossible to keep fluids down?
Did you drink untreated water, or eat cut fruit or food from a roadside stall during the trip?
Have you had malaria before, or taken any antimalarial tablets recently?
Has there been any confusion, unusual drowsiness or difficulty staying awake?
Did you sleep outdoors, or without a mosquito net, at night during the trip?
